|roster_url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/2024-25 |access-date= }} ==Regular season== ===November=== ====Cleveland State==== On November 4, Michigan began the season with a 101–53 victory over [[2024–25 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]]. Michigan was led by [[Danny Wolf]] with a game-high 19 points, 13 rebounds, three blocks and three steals for a double-double. [[Tre Donaldson]] had 16 points and seven assists, [[Will Tschetter]] scored 15 points, L.J. Cason had a career-high 14 points, [[Roddy Gayle Jr.]] had 13 points and Sam Walters added ten points. Michigan finished the first half on a 22–5 run and led 54–26 at halftime. Michigan shot 68.4% from the field, the second-best [[field goal percentage]] in program history, just shy of the record of 69.2% set against [[Alaska Anchorage Seawolves|Alaska-Anchorage]] on December 30, 1986.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/4/mens-basketball-u-m-wins-big-over-cleveland-state-to-begin-dusty-may-era |title=U-M Wins Big Over Cleveland State to Begin Dusty May Era |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 4, 2024 |access-date=November 4, 2024}} ====Wake Forest==== On November 10, Michigan lost to [[2024–25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]] 72–70 in the Deacon-Wolverine Challenge at the [[Greensboro Complex]]. The game was a neutral court matchup, despite [[Greensboro]] being 30 minutes from the [[Wake Forest University]] campus. Michigan was led by Gayle Jr. with 11 points, four rebounds and two assists, while Donaldson added ten points and a then career-high nine rebounds, and Cason added ten points.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/10/mens-basketball-u-m-drops-tight-game-against-wake-forest |title=U-M Drops Tight Game Against Wake Forest in Deacon-Wolverine Challenge |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 10, 2024 |access-date=November 10, 2024}} ====TCU==== On November 15, Michigan defeated [[2024–25 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]] 76–64. Michigan was led by [[Nimari Burnett]] with 16 points and six rebounds, while Wolf scored 14 points and 14 rebounds, his second double-double of the season. Donaldson also added 14 points and Walters had ten points. Michigan's defense held TCU to 34 percent shooting and 26 percent from behind the three-point line, while shooting 50 percent from the field themselves.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/15/mens-basketball-u-m-holds-off-tcu-to-kick-off-homestand |title=U-M Holds Off TCU to Kick Off Homestand |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 15, 2024 |access-date=November 15, 2024}} ====Miami (Ohio)==== On November 18, Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami (OH)]] 94–67. Michigan was led by Burnett with a game-high 18 points, Donaldson scored 16 points, Cason added 11 points and Gayle Jr. had ten points and five assists. With eight points in the game, [[Vladislav Goldin]] scored 1,200 career points and won his 100th career game.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/18/mens-basketball-strong-second-half-powers-michigan-to-94-67-win-over-miami-ohio |title=Strong Second Half Powers U-M to Lopsided Win Over Miami (Ohio) |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 18, 2024 |access-date=November 18, 2024}} ====Tarleton State==== On November 21, Michigan defeated [[Tarleton State Texans men's basketball|Tarleton State]] 72–49. Gayle Jr. had a game-high 16 points, while Donaldson and Walters each scored 13 points and Goldin added 12 points. With three blocks during the game, Goldin reached 150 for his career. Michigan held Tarleton State to 19 points in the second half, the lowest points allowed in any half this season.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/21/mens-basketball-u-m-completes-homestand-with-victory-over-tarleton-state |title=U-M Completes Homestand With Victory Over Tarleton State |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 21, 2024 |access-date=November 21, 2024}} ====Virginia Tech==== On November 25, Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] 75–63 in the Beach Division semifinal of the [[Fort Myers Tip-Off]]. Michigan was led by Gayle Jr. with a game-high 20 points, four rebounds and four assists, while Tschetter scored ten points and Wolf added four points and eleven rebounds. Michigan's defense forced 19 turnovers during the game.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/25/mens-basketball-michigan-downs-virginia-tech-in-fort-myers-tip-off |title=Michigan Downs Virginia Tech in Fort Myers Tip-Off |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 25, 2024 |access-date=November 25, 2024}} ====Xavier==== On November 27, Michigan upset No. 22 [[2024–25 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]] in the Fort Myers Tip-Off Beach Division Championship, winning 78–53. The Wolverines finished the game on a 20–4 run over the final nine minutes, and held Xavier without a field goal in the final seven minutes of the game.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/11/27/mens-basketball-strong-defensive-showing-propels-michigan-past-no-22-xavier-to-win-fort-myers-tip-off-championship |title=Strong Defensive Showing Propels Michigan Past No. 22 Xavier to Win Fort Myers Tip-Off Championship |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 27, 2024 |access-date=November 27, 2024}} Michigan was 6–1 through November.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/11/27/michigan-basketball-takes-down-no-22-xavier-to-win-fort-myers-tip-off-title/76619810007/ |title=Michigan basketball routs No. 22 Xavier to win Fort Myers Tip-Off title |work=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=November 27, 2024 |access-date=November 27, 2024}} Wolf had a game-high 20 points and 14 rebounds, his third double-double of the season. Goldin had 18 points, five rebounds and two blocks, and Donaldson added 13 points and three assists. Michigan's defense forced 19 turnovers for a consecutive game in the tournament, and the offense shot 11 of 22 (50%) from three-point range.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401729802/xavier-michigan|title=Fort Myers Tip-Off - Beach Division Championship (Michigan v. Xavier 2024-25) |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 27, 2024 |access-date=November 27, 2024}} ===December=== ====Wisconsin==== On December 3, Michigan opened the [[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten Conference season]] on the road against undefeated (8–0) No. 11 [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]], defeating the Badgers 67–64 to win their sixth consecutive game. Michigan was led by their big men Goldin and Wolf.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/03/michigan-basketball-stuns-wisconsin-67-64-despite-frigid-1st-half/76752779007/ |title=7-footers lift Michigan basketball after brutal start to 67-64 upset of No. 11 Wisconsin|work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}} Goldin had a game and a then career-high 24 points, five rebounds and three blocked shots. With his five rebounds, Goldin surpassed 700 in his career. Wolf scored 20 points, a team-high seven rebounds and a game-high five assists, three steals and five blocked shots; the five blocked shots being a then career-high. Michigan finished the game scoring six unanswered points, all by Goldin over the final 2:30. The game was a defensive battle, with the Wolverines shooting 39 percent from the field and 24 percent from three-point territory, while the Badgers were held to 34 percent from the field and 22 percent from three. Michigan finished the game with eleven blocked shots, their first game with more than ten blocks since November 23, 2022. The victory marked the 100th win versus Wisconsin in Michigan basketball history, improving to 100–75 in the all-time series.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/3/mens-basketball-u-m-defeats-no-11-wisconsin-to-start-big-ten-action |title=U-M Defeats No. 11 Wisconsin to Start Big Ten Action |first=Shira |last=Black |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721306|title=Goldin helps Michigan beat No. 11 Wisconsin 67-64 as Badgers take their 1st loss|website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}} It was also only the fourth win in Madison (in twenty games) this millennium. The three previous Michigan teams each won the Big Ten.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2024/12/michigan-basketball-opens-big-ten-play-with-rare-win-at-wisconsin.html?outputType=amp|title=Michigan basketball opens Big Ten play with rare win at Wisconsin|website=[[MLive.com]] |date=December 3, 2024 |access-date=December 3, 2024}} ====Iowa==== On December 7, Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] 85–83, winning a seventh consecutive game. The Wolverines were led by Goldin with a game-high 20 points and 11 rebounds, earning him his first double-double of the season and the Big Ten Player of the Week (along with the Wisconsin game).{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/9/2024-25-michigan-mens-basketball-awards-and-honors |title=Awards and Honors: Goldin Earns B1G Player of the Week |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 9, 2024 |access-date=December 9, 2024}} Wolf had 13 points and 14 rebounds, his fourth double-double of the season. Donaldson added a then career-high 18 points and five assists, Gayle Jr. had 17 points and five assists, and Tschetter added 13 points. Michigan gave up 19 points off 17 turnovers. The Wolverines led by as many as 11 points in the second half, and went over five and a half minutes without a field goal. Iowa used a 17–7 run to tie the game with 16 seconds remaining. Gayle Jr. scored the game-winning basket with 4.6 seconds remaining in the game, after the Hawkeyes were called for [[Goaltending (basketball)|goaltending]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/7/mens-basketball-michigan-holds-off-iowa-to-close-early-big-ten-slate |title=Michigan Holds Off Iowa to Close Early Big Ten Slate |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 7, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721312 |title=Gayle scores late to give Michigan 85-83 win over Iowa for Wolverines' 7th straight victory |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 7, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024}} Michigan's seven game win streak was the longest since winning 11 consecutive games to start the [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2020–21 season]]. Improving to 8–1, the Wolverines' matched their win total from the [[2023–24 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|previous season]], 8–24.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/07/michigan-basketball-game-score-recap-tre-donaldson-vlad-goldin/76841830007/ |title=No. 23 Michigan basketball holds off Iowa, 85-83, for 7th straight victory: 'Not surprised' |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=December 7, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024}} ====Arkansas==== On December 9, Michigan was ranked No. 14 in the [[AP poll]]. It marked the first time the Wolverines were ranked in the AP poll since November 14, 2022, and the first time inside the top 15 since November 15, 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/michigan-wolverines/news/michigan-wolverines-basketball-ranked-in-ap-poll-for-first-time-since-2022/|title=Amid seven-game win streak, Michigan basketball ranked in AP poll for first time since 2022 |website=On3.com |first=Clayton |last=Sayfie |date=December 9, 2024 |access-date=December 9, 2024}} Michigan was also ranked No. 14 in the [[coaches poll]], entering the poll at No. 23 the previous week.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2024/12/michigan-basketball-rides-win-streak-title-into-top-25-rankings.html |title=Michigan basketball rides win streak, title into top-25 rankings |website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=December 9, 2024 |access-date=December 9, 2024}} On December 10, Michigan played [[2024–25 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]] in the [[Jimmy V Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York City]], losing to the Razorbacks 89–87. Michigan opened the game leading by as many as 15 points in the first half, before Arkansas cut the lead to four at halftime. The loss snapped a seven-game winning streak for the Wolverines, and an eleven-game winning streak for Michigan at Madison Square Garden dating back to 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2024/12/10/michigan-basketball-game-score-vs-arkansas-89-87-loss-madison-square-garden/76904143007/ |title=Michigan basketball blows 15-point lead, falls to Arkansas 89-87 in NYC: 'Cannot stop playing' |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=December 10, 2024 |access-date=December 10, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2024/12/10/mens-basketball-michigan-falls-short-at-buzzer-against-arkansas-at-madison-square-garden |title=Michigan Falls Short at Buzzer Against Arkansas at Madison Square Garden |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=December 10, 2024 |access-date=December 11, 2024}} Goldin was the Wolverines' leading scorer for a third consecutive game, totaling 17 points, nine rebounds and two blocks. Wolf scored 14 points, nine rebounds, and a career-high nine assists, just missing a [[triple-double]]. Gayle Jr. and Tschetter each added 13 points, and Burnett added ten points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401727356 |title=Arkansas holds off No. 14 Michigan 89-87 in Jimmy V Classic at MSG |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 10, 2024 |access-date=December 10, 2024}} ====Oklahoma==== On December 18, No. 24 Michigan lost to undefeated No. 14 [[2024–25 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] 87–86 in the [[Jumpman Invitational]] at the [[Spectrum Center]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]]. Michigan in turn went on a 9–0 run to go up 73–65 with 5:09 to play, and USC answered with a 6–0 run to get within two points, but Michigan finished the game on a 10–0 run to secure the victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/01/04/michigan-basketball-game-score-recap-southern-cal-danny-wolf/77462553007/ |title=Michigan basketball catches waves — three of them — en route to 85-74 win over USC |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=January 4, 2025 |access-date=January 4, 2025}} ====UCLA==== On January 7, No. 24 Michigan remained in Los Angeles against No. 22 [[2024–25 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]], their fourth ranked opponent of the season and the second top 25 matchup.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/01/07/michigan-basketball-eyes-signature-win-vs-extremely-physical-ucla/77493165007/|title=Predicting Michigan basketball's top 25 showdown vs 'extremely physical' UCLA|work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=January 7, 2025 |access-date=January 7, 2025}} The Wolverines defeated the Bruins 94–75, remaining undefeated both on the road and in the conference. Michigan was led by Goldin with a career-high 36 points and seven rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/01/08/michigans-vladislav-goldin-scores-career-high-36-in-94-75-win-at-ucla/77528154007/ |title=Michigan's Vladislav Goldin scores career-high 36 points in 94-75 victory at UCLA |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=January 8, 2025}} It was the most points scored by a Wolverine since [[Daniel Horton (basketball)|Daniel Horton]] posted 39 on February 21, 2006.{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/bltd68729cc7de90b47/|title=Iowa, Michigan, USC Score Men's Basketball Weekly Accolades|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=January 13, 2025|access-date=January 13, 2025}} Against the four ranked teams Michigan played to date, Goldin averaged 26.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 2.25 blocks and shot 70.9 percent from the floor. Michigan shot 61.5 percent from the field, including (15 of 28) on three-point attempts.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/01/michigan-beats-ucla-to-sweep-los-angeles-trip-stay-perfect-in-big-ten.html?outputType=amp|title=Michigan beats UCLA to sweep Los Angeles trip, stay perfect in Big Ten |website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=January 8, 2025}} The Wolverines led by as many as 18 points in the first half, before leading 47–37 at halftime. Michigan responded with a 19–6 run, as UCLA went over seven minutes without a field goal.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721338 |title=No. 24 Michigan shuts down UCLA's second half rally to beat 22nd-ranked Bruins 94-75 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=January 8, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/1/8/mens-basketball-goldin-donaldson-shine-as-michigan-tops-no-22-ucla-to-complete-west-coast-sweep |title=Goldin, Donaldson Shine as Michigan Tops No. 22 UCLA to Complete West Coast Sweep |website=MGoBlue.com |date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=January 8, 2025}} The 94 points scored on UCLA were the most the Bruins had allowed all season.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6047193/2025/01/08/mick-cronin-ucla-loss-michigan/#:~:text=The%2094%20points%20scored%20by,they%20are%2C”%20Cronin%20said.|title=UCLA's Mick Cronin lambasts team for being 'soft' and 'delusional' after 19-point loss to Michigan|work=[[The New York Times]] ([[The Athletic]]) |last1=Williams |first1=Justin |date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=January 8, 2025 }} ====Washington==== On January 12, No. 24 Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] 91–75, staying unbeaten in their fifth conference game. It was the Wolverines best start to Big Ten play since the [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2020–21 team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2025/01/12/michigan-basketball-uses-balanced-attack-to-roll-past-washington/77650336007/|title=Michigan basketball uses balanced attack to roll past Washington|work=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=January 12, 2024 |access-date=January 12, 2024 }} Michigan was led by Goldin with 19 points and seven rebounds, which earned him the Co-Big Ten Player of the Week (along with the UCLA game). The Wolverines led the Huskies, 48–38, at halftime and finished the game shooting 52.7 percent from the floor with (11 of 29) on three-point shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721349 |title=Goldin, Burnett lead No. 24 Michigan to 91-75 win over Washington |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 11, 2025 |access-date=January 11, 2025}} ====Minnesota==== On January 16, No. 20 Michigan lost on the road to [[2024–25 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]], 84–81, in overtime. It was the Wolverines' first conference loss and first road loss of the season, and the Golden Gophers' first conference win.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2025/01/16/minnesota-stuns-michigan-with-buzzer-beating-3-pointer-in-overtime/77745374007/|title='We overlooked them': Minnesota stuns Michigan with buzzer-beating 3-pointer in overtime|work=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=January 16, 2024 |access-date=January 16, 2024}} Michigan was led by Wolf scoring a season-high 23 points and recording team-highs with ten rebounds and seven assists; his eighth double-double of the season. Michigan finished the game shooting 37 percent from the floor, (6 of 29) from three and committed a season-high 22 turnovers. Michigan was led by Goldin with 14 points, while Burnett, Donaldson and Gayle Jr. added 11 points each.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721378 |title=Braden Smith flirts with triple-double in No. 11 Purdue's 91-64 victory over No. 21 Michigan |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=January 24, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/1/24/mens-basketball-u-m-falls-on-the-road-to-no-11-purdue |title=U-M Falls on the Road to No. 11 Purdue|first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |website=MGoBlue.com |date=January 24, 2025 |access-date=January 24, 2025}} ====Penn State==== On January 27, Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]] 76–72, improving to 10–0 at home. Michigan was led by Donaldson with a career-high 21 points, seven assists and a career-high tying four steals. Wolf added 11 points and nine rebounds, while Burnett scored ten points. Goldin was limited in minutes due to an illness. The Wolverines and Nittany Lions were tied 35–35 at halftime. Michigan opened the second half on a 12–5 run and went on to lead 64–57 with just over seven minutes to play. Penn State answered with a 15–3 run to take a 72–67 lead with two minutes remaining. Michigan was led by Wolf with 16 points, 14 rebounds, four blocks and two steals, his ninth double-double of the season. He tied [[Brooks Barnhizer]] and [[Julian Reese]] for the most double-doubles in the Big Ten. Goldin scored 14 points (surpassing 1,500 career points), and Donaldson added ten points and six assists.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/2/1/mens-basketball-defense-powers-u-m-to-narrow-victory-at-rutgers |title=Defense Powers U-M to Narrow Victory at Rutgers |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=February 1, 2025 |access-date=February 1, 2025}} The Wolverines led the Scarlet Knights 32–25 at halftime, their second lowest points allowed in the first half this season. Michigan held the lead the entire second half, though never by more than single-digits; Rutgers scored a three-point shot as time expired. They limited Rutgers to 32.8 percent from the floor, including holding the Big Ten's leading scorer at the time, [[Ace Bailey (basketball)|Ace Bailey]], to ten points on (3 of 15) shooting.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401721397 |title=Wolf records double-double to lead Michigan to 66-63 win over Rutgers |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=February 1, 2025 |access-date=February 1, 2025}} ====Oregon==== On February 5, No. 24 Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] 80–76, sweeping the four Big Ten newcomers from the [[Pac-12 Conference]] and improving to 11–0 at home.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/02/michigan-basketball-beats-oregon-to-keep-pace-in-big-ten-title-chase.html?outputType=amp|title=Michigan basketball beats Oregon to keep pace in Big Ten title chase |website=[[Mlive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=February 5, 2025 |access-date=February 5, 2025}} The Wolverines were led by Tschetter with a season-high 17 points off the bench and Wolf with 15 points and 12 rebounds, his Big Ten leading tenth double-double of the season. It was the program's first victory against a top ten ranked team at home since defeating No. 3 [[2021–22 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] on February 10, 2022. The 12 straight wins at Crisler Center also tied the Wolverines' best home record to start a season since the 2020–21 team.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/2/11/mens-basketball-u-m-downs-no-7-purdue-late-to-top-big-ten-standings |title=U-M Downs No. 7 Purdue Late to Top Big Ten Standings |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |date=February 11, 2025 |access-date=February 11, 2025}} Michigan was led by Wolf with 15 points and nine rebounds, Gayle Jr. had 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench, while Goldin and Donaldson each scored 12 points. The Wolverines finished the game shooting 44.6 percent from the field, (7 of 23) on three-point attempts, tied the Boilermakers in turnovers with 11, but had a season-low team assist total in consecutive games with seven.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721420 |title=Wolf scores 15 and No. 20 holds off No. 7 Purdue 75-73 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=February 11, 2025 |access-date=February 11, 2025}} ====Ohio State==== On February 16, No. 20 Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in their [[Michigan–Ohio State men's basketball rivalry|rivalry]] game 86–83, winning a sixth consecutive game and improving to 20–5, 12–2 in the Big Ten and 6–2 on the road. Michigan finished the game shooting 46 percent from the field, (5 of 21) from three-point territory, were out rebounded 34 to a season-low 25 (14 to 7 on offensive rebounds), and lost the turnover battle 14 to 11.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401721444 |title=Richardson scores 21 and No. 14 Michigan State tops No. 12 Michigan 75-62 for 1st place in Big Ten |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=February 21, 2025 |access-date=February 21, 2025}} Before the game, Dusty May agreed to a contract extension with the university.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/2/21/mens-basketball-manuel-may-come-to-terms-on-new-multi-year-agreement |title=Manuel, May Come to Terms on New Multi-Year Agreement |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=February 21, 2025 |access-date=February 21, 2025}} ====Nebraska==== On February 24, No. 15 Michigan defeated [[2024–25 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 49–46, moving into a tie with Michigan State atop the Big Ten standings at 13–3 and improving to 7–2 on the road. The Wolverines finished the game shooting 51.7 percent from the floor, 8-of-26 on three point attempts, had 25 team assists and a season-low six turnovers.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/14/mens-basketball-second-half-push-guides-michigan-past-purdue-into-big-ten-tourney-semifinals |title=Second-Half Push Guides Michigan Past Purdue, Into B1G Tourney Semifinals |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 14, 2025 |access-date=March 14, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743939 |title=No. 22 Michigan snaps skid with 86-68 win over No. 20 Purdue, advances to Big Ten semis |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 14, 2025 |access-date=March 14, 2025}} With 23 wins on the season, [[Dusty May]] tied [[Steve Fisher (basketball)|Steve Fisher]] for the second-most total wins in program history by a first-year head coach.{{cite web|url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/2024/4/2/24117495/michigan-wolverines-head-coach-college-basketball-juwan-howard-john-beilein-dusty-may |title=A history of first-year head coaches at Michigan as the Dusty May era begins |website=Maizenbrew.com |first=Daniel |last=Plocher |date=April 2, 2024 |access-date=March 14, 2025}} ====Semifinal==== On March 15, No. 22 Michigan defeated No. 11 Maryland in the semifinal 81–80, advancing to their sixth Big Ten championship game. Michigan was led by Goldin with 25 points and ten rebounds, his sixth double-double of the season and fifth game scoring 25 points or more. Wolf had 21 points and 14 rebounds, his Big Ten leading fifteenth double-double. Donaldson scored 12 points with a career-high nine assists, including the game-winning shot, and [[Nimari Burnett]] added ten points. Rubin Jones surpassed 1,000 career points with his only field goal. The Wolverines led the Terrapins 38–34 at halftime, courtesy of a 22–11 run to end the half. Michigan opened the second half on a 11–0 run (18–0 run in combination with seven straight points to end the first half). Maryland answered with a 10–0 run and another 14–0 run to take the lead with 8:21 remaining in the game. After trading baskets over the final eight minutes, Maryland's [[Derik Queen]] made two free throws with 5.3 seconds remaining to give the Terrapins an 80–79 lead; with no timeouts remaining for Michigan. Donaldson responded and went the length of the court, scoring a left-handed layup with 0.4 seconds remaining to win the game. Michigan finished the semifinal shooting 47 percent from the floor, 7-of-18 on three-point attempts, out rebounded Maryland 47 to 18, but lost the turnover battle 19 to six.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/15/mens-basketball-donaldsons-last-second-layup-sends-michigan-to-big-ten-title-game |title=Donaldson's Last-Second Layup Sends Michigan to Big Ten Title Game |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743941 |title=Donaldson's court-length drive sends No. 22 Michigan past No. 11 Maryland 81-80 in Big Ten tourney |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2025}} The Wolverines won their twelfth conference game by four points or fewer, the most by any team in any league in the history of college basketball.{{cite web|url=https://x.com/MattNorlander/status/1901048825902744057?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet |title=CBS Sports Research |first=Matt |last=Norlander |website=[[Twitter|X]] |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2025}} ====Championship==== On March 16, No. 22 Michigan defeated No. 18 [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the Big Ten championship game 59–53, winning a fourth tournament and the first since [[2018 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2018]]. The Wolverines improved to 25–9, 17–6 against conference opponents and 7–5 versus ranked opponents. Michigan was led by Goldin with 11 points and five rebounds, who was awarded the Most Outstanding Player of the tournament. Wolf joined Goldin on the All-Tournament team.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-wins-2025-big-ten-tournament-championship-over-wisconsin |title=U-M Downs No. 18 Wisconsin to Capture B1G Tournament Title |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/michigan-win-big-ten-title-after-beating-wisconsin/ |title=Michigan rallies to beat Wisconsin 59-53 for Big Ten title |website=CBS News |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} Donaldson also had 11 points and eight assists, the second most assists in his career. The Wolverines trailed the Badgers 23–21 at halftime, their lowest points scored in any half this season. Both teams shot 17 percent in the half from three-point range on a combined 7-of-41. In the second half, after being down 38–27 with 13 minutes remaining, Michigan used two separate 7–0 runs to tie the game 45–45 with just under six minutes. The Wolverines closed the game out on a 11–2 run to secure their Big Ten title, including 6-of-6 at the free throw line for their final points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401743942/wisconsin-michigan |title=No. 22 Michigan v. No. 18 Wisconsin (Big Ten Tournament Final) |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} With 25 wins on the season, May tied [[Brian Ellerbe]] for the most total wins in program history by a first-year head coach. He also became the first officially recognized conference coach to win the Big Ten tournament title in their first season, with the only other being Ellerbe in Michigan's first tournament win in [[1998 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|1998]]; though that season was later vacated by the NCAA. Michigan finished as Big Ten champions one year after finishing in last place at No. 14 in the conference, an increase of 14 total conference wins.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/michigan/news/michigan-basketball-coach-dusty-may-makes-undeniable-history-big-ten-tournament-final-vs-wisconsin-badgers/46092fd706476b0f8d4d392b |title=Michigan basketball coach Dusty May makes undeniable history in Big Ten Tournament final vs. Wisconsin Badgers |website=[[The Sporting News]] |first=Zain |last=Bando |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} ===NCAA tournament=== On March 16, Michigan received an automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the South Region. It was their first NCAA tournament appearance since [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-receives-ncaa-no-5-seed-will-face-uc-san-diego-in-denver |title=Michigan Receives NCAA No. 5 Seed, Will Face UC San Diego in Denver |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 16, 2025}} ====First Round==== On March 20, the Wolverines defeated No. 12 seed [[2024–25 UC San Diego Tritons men's basketball team|UC San Diego]], 68–65, in the First Round in [[Denver|Denver, Colorado]]. The Wolverines improved to 26–9 and won a fourth consecutive postseason game. Michigan was led by Goldin with 14 points and seven rebounds, Donaldson had 12 points with seven rebounds, and Gayle Jr. scored 11 points. The Wolverines opened the game with a 10–0 run, leading the Tritons 41–27 at halftime. UCSD opened the second half on a 17–4 run, cutting the score to 45–44. Michigan answered with a 14–5 run, before UCSD rallied with a 16–4 run of their own to take their first lead of the game, 65–63 with 2:29 remaining. Donaldson hit a three-point shot to retake the lead and Goldin closed the game out with two free throws to secure the victory. The Wolverines finished the game shooting 42.1 percent from the floor, 9-of-27 on three-point attempts, but had 14 turnovers and made 11-of-20 of their free throw attempts during the game. With 26 wins, May became the winningest first-year head coach in program history.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/20/mens-basketball-u-m-fends-off-uc-san-diego-in-ncaa-tournament-first-round-matchup |title=U-M Fends Off UC San Diego in NCAA Tournament First-Round Matchup |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 20, 2025 |access-date=March 20, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401745963 |title=No. 5 seed Michigan holds off UC San Diego 68-65 in March Madness nailbiter |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 20, 2025 |access-date=March 20, 2025}} ====Second Round==== On March 22, No. 5 seed Michigan defeated No. 4 seed [[2024–25 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the Second Round 91–79, earning a sixth Sweet Sixteen appearance in the last eight NCAA tournaments and winning a fifth consecutive postseason game. Michigan was led by Gayle Jr. with a season-high 26 points off the bench (4-of-6 on three-point shots), and Goldin with 23 points, 12 rebounds and three blocks; his seventh double-double of the season. Wolf added 14 points, nine rebounds and three blocks, while Cason had 11 points. After six lead changes, the Wolverines trailed the Aggies 39–35 at halftime. In the second half, Michigan went down 57–47 with just over 13 minutes remaining before rallying to take their first lead of the half at the six minute mark, 71–70, courtesy of Gayle Jr. with 12 straight team points (21 total points in the half). The Wolverines never surrendered the lead and scored 20 points in the final six minutes, ending with a 9–0 run to secure the comeback win. Michigan finished the game shooting 43.1 percent from the floor, 6-of-22 on three-point attempts, 29-of-36 on free throws, out rebounded the Aggies 48 to 39, and had only nine turnovers.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/22/mens-basketball-gayle-leads-u-ms-second-half-rally-against-texas-am-wolverines-off-to-sweet-16 |title=Gayle Leads U-M's Second-Half Rally Against Texas A&M; Wolverines off to Sweet 16 |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |website=MGoBlue.com |date=March 22, 2025 |access-date=March 22, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401746036 |title=Roddy Gayle's second-half surge leads Michigan past Texas A&M 91-79 in March Madness turnaround |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 22, 2025 |access-date=March 22, 2025}} No team in NCAA history has lost as many games the season before and advanced to the Sweet Sixteen the next year (since introduced in 1975).{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/michigans-march-madness-turnaround-under-dusty-may-shows-why-hes-one-of-the-nations-elite-coaches |title=Michigan's March Madness turnaround under Dusty May shows why he's one of the nation's elite coaches |first=Cameron |last=Salerno |website=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 22, 2025 |access-date=March 23, 2025}} ====Sweet Sixteen==== On March 28, No. 5 seed Michigan was defeated by the No. 1 overall seed [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]], 78–65, in the Sweet Sixteen in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]]. The Wolverines trailed the Tigers 30–29 at halftime, before opening the second half on a 19–9 run to lead 48–39 with 12:26 remaining. Auburn then went on a 28–6 run (including 12–0 to start) to regain the lead, 67–54, before closing the game out in the final minutes. Michigan was led by Wolf with 20 points and six rebounds, leading him to a South Region all-tournament team selection.{{cite web|url=https://auburnwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/auburn/mens-basketball/2025/03/31/auburn-basketball-march-madness-all-south-team-johni-broome-tahaad-pettiford/82737959007/ |title=Auburn duo earns NCAA Tournament All-South Region team honors |first=Taylor |last=Jones |website=[[USA Today]] |date=March 31, 2025 |access-date=April 3, 2025}} Goldin and Burnett each added ten points, and Gayle Jr. surpassed 1,000 career points by scoring seven points. The Wolverines shot 35.6 percent from the floor, 5-of-17 from three-point range, were out rebounded 48 to 33 (including giving up 19 offensive rebounds), had 15 turnovers and a season-low six team assists.
